title: Military Rehabilitation and Compensation Amendment (Single Treatment Pathway) Bill 2019
short_title: Military Rehabilitation and Compensation Amendment (Single Treatment Pathway) Bill 2019

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would replace two medical treatment pathways under military compensation legislation with a single system using Department of Veterans’ Affairs health cards.
Eligible veterans would access treatment through their cards rather than routinely paying first and seeking reimbursement, with a compensation exception for special circumstances.
The changes would start on 1 July 2019 and validate earlier transfers between pathways and certain payments already made to treatment providers.
changes: The Commission would no longer have to choose a treatment pathway after assessing a person’s needs.
Reasonable treatment costs incurred before an entitlement decision could still be compensated.
Compensation for the same treatment could not be paid twice under the new reimbursement provisions.
summary.affected: Veterans eligible for military compensation treatment, the Military Rehabilitation and Compensation Commission and treatment providers are affected.

speeches.speaker: Karen Andrews
speeches.brief: The bill removes the dual treatment pathway and introduces a single treatment pathway via a DVA health card, allowing veterans to access treatment without up-front costs or claim forms, with around 4,000 clients no longer needing to seek reimbursement.
